name: PBB Relay
shortDescription: Selective store-and-forward delivery for approved messages and operational events between configured PBB nodes.
longDescription: PBB Relay accepts approved message envelopes, persists them locally, and retries delivery through configured routes. It supports selected inter-node workflows without requiring every application database to stay continuously connected.
Relay is a message transport, not universal database replication. Each producer and consumer owns its message contract, authorization, idempotency, retention, and business-state handling.

readiness.note: Store-and-forward envelopes, retry handling, delivery state, and selected module integrations are implemented.
remainingWork: Finalize topology-specific token ownership and rotation.
Publish retention, retry, quarantine, and recovery runbooks.
Load-test each approved route and message contract before field rollout.

nodeRole: Provides durable selective delivery between known endpoints so supported workflows can queue locally and resume when an approved route becomes reachable.
localBehavior: Accepted envelopes and delivery state remain in the local Relay store.
Workers can retry pending routes without changing the producer application database.
connectivityBehavior: Delivery resumes only across explicitly configured and reachable routes.
Relay does not merge arbitrary records or create a shared mutable database.
operationalConsiderations: Monitor queue age, quarantine, attempts, and destination health.
Set retention and replay policy per message contract and deployment topology.
securityBoundary: Authenticate producers, destinations, and operational webhook consumers.
Minimize envelope content and avoid treating transport acceptance as business acceptance.

faqs.question: Does Relay synchronize every PBB database?
faqs.answer: No. Relay sends only selected, approved messages. It does not copy entire databases or automatically combine records from different nodes.

faqs.question: What happens when the destination is unreachable?
faqs.answer: Relay can keep an accepted message on the local node and try again later, following the delivery and storage rules set for that deployment.

faqs.question: Who owns the meaning of a Relay message?
faqs.answer: The apps sending and receiving the message must agree on what it means, what information is allowed, who may use it, how duplicates are handled, and what action should follow.

faqs.question: Can Relay send through any available internet route?
faqs.answer: No. Deployment owners must approve where messages may go, how Relay connects, which credentials it uses, and which kinds of messages it may send.

faqs.question: What should operators monitor?
faqs.answer: Operators should watch how long messages are waiting, repeated delivery attempts, rejected messages, the health of receiving services, storage limits, and confirmation that messages were acted on.
